units.tip: Most people in the UK use a current account for everyday money and pay by debit card, phone or bank transfer. Cheques are now rare. Banks are regulated, and savings are protected by a government-backed scheme (the FSCS) up to a limit.

s.a: A current account is where your pay goes in and your bills come out.
s.b: Like a locked drawer behind the counter. Only you have the key.

s.a: Your card is linked to your account. When you pay, the money leaves your account straight away.
s.b: Like handing over cash, but you don’t have to carry the cash.

s.a: You can see your money in the app, on the website, or at a cash machine.
s.b: Like asking the cashier for your balance, but open 24 hours a day.

s.b: Like the address of the building.

s.a: An account number has 8 numbers. It points to your account and nobody else’s.
s.b: Like the number on your drawer inside.

s.a: To get paid, give your name, sort code and account number. Never give your PIN.
s.b: Like writing your details on a paying-in slip.

s.b: Like a safe that the government backs up.

s.a: Scammers pretend to be your bank. They call, text or email.
s.b: In a branch, you can see the person helping you.

guides.sum: A UK current account is where your money lives day to day. You get a debit card, a sort code and an account number. Your savings are protected, up to a limit.
pts: Your pay goes into your current account. Your bills and shopping come out of it.
You pay with a debit card, your phone or a bank transfer. Cheques are rare now.
Your sort code (6 numbers) and account number (8 numbers) are how people pay you.
Never share your PIN or your full password. Not with anyone.
UK banks follow strict rules. Savings are protected by a scheme called the FSCS, up to a limit.
In a branch you talk to a person. In the app you do the same jobs yourself, at any time.
words: The account you use every day
A card that takes money from your account
A scheme that protects savings, up to a limit
guides.rem: If you are not sure, stop and ask. A real bank never minds questions.

guides.sum: The NatWest app is a bank branch on your phone. You can check your balance, pay people and get help at any time.
pts: Download it only from your phone’s official app store. Check that it says NatWest.
Log in, then set Face ID, a fingerprint or a passcode so it is quick next time.
Your balance is at the top. Below it is a list of money in and money out.
To pay someone, you need their name, sort code and account number. Check every number.
Turn on alerts. You get a message when money comes in or goes out.
If something looks wrong, use Help in the app.
words: How much money you have now
Press to say yes, go ahead
guides.rem: Take your time. You can always stop before you press Confirm.

guides.sum: Online banking is the same account as the app, on a bigger screen. Always check the address says natwest.com.
pts: Type natwest.com into your browser. Do not click links in texts or emails.
Look for the padlock and natwest.com in the address bar.
You may get a code by text. This is normal. The code is only for you.
Open Statements to read or download your monthly statements.
Open Settings to change your phone number or address.
Log out when you finish, especially on a shared computer.
words: The program you use to open websites
A sign the connection is safe
A record of your money in and out
Close your account when you finish
guides.rem: Only you should ever use your codes.

guides.sum: Scammers pretend to be your bank. Your bank will never ask for your PIN, or ask you to move money to a “safe account”.
pts: Scammers can call, text or email. They sound kind, and in a hurry.
Your bank will never ask for your PIN or your full password.
Your bank will never ask you to move money to a “safe account”.
If you are unsure, hang up. Call the number on the back of your card.
Never read out a code from a text to someone who rang you.
You can walk into a branch, or use Help in the app, at any time.
words: A trick to steal your money
A fake text or email that looks real
A lie scammers use. There is no such thing
End the call. You are allowed to
guides.rem: Real banks never rush you. If you feel rushed, stop.
